binaryprimitives-endian.title: Read and write explicit endianness with BinaryPrimitives
binaryprimitives-endian.short: Convert integers and bytes without temporary arrays
binaryprimitives-endian.summary: BinaryPrimitives reads and writes integer values on spans with an explicit big- or little-endian byte order.
binaryprimitives-endian.why: It makes a protocol or file format's byte order visible in code and avoids combining BitConverter with manual byte reversal.
binaryprimitives-endian.tips: Confirm the byte order required by the format and ensure enough input bytes are available before reading.

utf8parser-span.title: Parse UTF-8 bytes directly with Utf8Parser
utf8parser-span.short: Read values without first creating a string
utf8parser-span.summary: Utf8Parser.TryParse parses values directly from a UTF-8 ReadOnlySpan<byte> and reports how many bytes it consumed.
utf8parser-span.why: It avoids converting UTF-8 input to string first in allocation-sensitive parsing paths.
utf8parser-span.tips: Check both success and consumed; when the whole input must be a value, reject trailing unconsumed data.

memorymappedfile-view.title: Access large files through MemoryMappedFile views
memorymappedfile-view.short: Map a file and work with only the needed region
memorymappedfile-view.summary: MemoryMappedFile maps file contents into virtual memory and exposes regions through views.
memorymappedfile-view.why: It can suit repeated random access to large files without loading the entire file into one byte array.
memorymappedfile-view.tips: Dispose both views and the mapping. For ordinary sequential reads, FileStream is usually simpler.

file-enumerate-lines-async.title: Process lines asynchronously with File.ReadLinesAsync
file-enumerate-lines-async.short: Use await foreach without retaining every line
file-enumerate-lines-async.summary: File.ReadLinesAsync exposes a text file as IAsyncEnumerable<string> and reads its lines asynchronously as enumeration advances.
file-enumerate-lines-async.why: Large text files can be processed as lines arrive instead of being loaded completely first.
file-enumerate-lines-async.tips: Pass a CancellationToken, and use ReadAllLinesAsync instead when you intentionally need all lines in memory.

json-extension-data.title: Preserve unknown JSON properties with JsonExtensionData
json-extension-data.short: Capture properties that are not in the model
json-extension-data.summary: A dictionary marked with JsonExtensionData receives JSON properties that did not bind to normal model properties.
json-extension-data.why: It helps preserve future or extension fields when reading and writing extensible payloads.
json-extension-data.tips: Treat extension values as untrusted input and validate their type and contents before using them.

httpclient-default-request-version.title: Set HttpClient's default HTTP version policy
httpclient-default-request-version.short: State the preferred HTTP version and fallback behavior
httpclient-default-request-version.summary: DefaultRequestVersion and DefaultVersionPolicy control the default requested HTTP version and negotiation policy.
httpclient-default-request-version.why: They make preferences such as HTTP/2 and whether lower versions are acceptable explicit.
httpclient-default-request-version.tips: The actual protocol depends on the server, transport, and policy. Inspect the response Version when it matters.

task-yield-ui-loop.title: Use Task.Yield to yield control during long async work
task-yield-ui-loop.short: Schedule the continuation instead of running it immediately
task-yield-ui-loop.summary: Awaiting Task.Yield schedules the continuation asynchronously and returns control to the caller for the moment.
task-yield-ui-loop.why: It can split long synchronous stretches in code such as UI work made of many small operations.
task-yield-ui-loop.tips: It does not reduce CPU work. For heavy computation, redesign the work or move it appropriately rather than sprinkling Task.Yield calls.

readonlysequence-segments.title: Process ReadOnlySequence<T> segment by segment
readonlysequence-segments.short: Read non-contiguous buffers without joining them first
readonlysequence-segments.summary: ReadOnlySequence<T> can represent data spread across multiple memory regions and can be enumerated by segment.
readonlysequence-segments.why: Data from APIs such as PipeReader can be processed without copying all segments into one large contiguous array.
readonlysequence-segments.tips: Never assume the sequence is a single segment. Design Span-based processing to handle each segment when possible.

arraypool-clear-return.title: Clear sensitive ArrayPool buffers when returning them
arraypool-clear-return.short: Do not leave secrets in reusable arrays
arraypool-clear-return.summary: ArrayPool.Return with clearArray: true clears an array before it is returned to the pool.
arraypool-clear-return.why: Pooled arrays may later be rented by other code, so sensitive contents should not remain in reusable storage.
arraypool-clear-return.tips: Clearing has a cost. Use it deliberately for buffers containing passwords, keys, or other sensitive material.

exception-inner-chain.title: Preserve InnerException when wrapping failures
exception-inner-chain.short: Add higher-level context without losing the original cause
exception-inner-chain.summary: When translating a low-level exception into a domain exception, passing the original exception preserves it as InnerException.
exception-inner-chain.why: Callers get useful higher-level context while diagnostics retain the underlying failure information.
exception-inner-chain.tips: If you only need to rethrow the same exception, use throw; and avoid unnecessary wrapping.
